strings.name: Joseph Stiglitz
strings.role: Economist · Asymmetric information and public policy
strings.summary: Joseph Stiglitz studies how unequal information changes market outcomes, helping economists reassess market efficiency and government’s role. He chaired the US Council of Economic Advisers and served as World Bank chief economist before continuing research and policy work at Columbia. He shared the 2001 economics Nobel with George Akerlof and Michael Spence and writes widely on globalization and inequality.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026, including a 2026 CV and interview. Selected research, public appointments and books are covered. The Nobel was shared; policy arguments are not presented as settled conclusions.
strings.influence.rationale: Researched asymmetric information and market failures and shaped debates on globalization, inequality and development.

strings.timeline.event-6.title: Initiative for Policy Dialogue

strings.timeline.event-7.title: World Bank chief economist

strings.timeline.event-8.title: Chairs White House economic advisers

strings.timeline.event-9.title: MIT doctorate
